title: Encrypted DNS Discovery RFC 9463 DHCPv6 OPTION_V6_DNR Wire Architecture
purpose: Define the RFC 9463 DHCPv6 OPTION_V6_DNR wire-format boundary for encrypted DNS discovery data.
design_summary: The DHCPv6 slice adds a pure OPTION_V6_DNR TLV codec that writes and parses the RFC 9463 option-code, option-length, service-priority, RFC 8415 DNS-name, IPv6 address-length/address list, and RFC 9460 SvcParams fields. It also exposes ORO request data, ADN-only mode, ALPN default-port lookup, multiple OPTION_V6_DNR decoding, service-priority sorting, and invalid-option discard behavior.
data_and_state_considerations: The helper is deterministic and allocation-light for control-plane option data. It does not own DHCP client state, network-interface selection, resolver installation, certificate validation, or DHCPv4/Neighbor Discovery codecs.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Only DHCPv6 OPTION_V6_DNR TLVs are decoded by this helper.
ADN-only mode omits Addr Length, IPv6 addresses, and SvcParams.
Populated options require non-zero Addr Length that is a multiple of 16.
IPv6 loopback and multicast addresses are discarded during decode, and an option with no usable address is invalid.
SvcParams reuse the RFC 9460 key/value codec and reject ipv4hint/ipv6hint.
Multiple OPTION_V6_DNR instances remain separate and are returned in service-priority order.
risks: This slice does not implement DHCPv4 OPTION_V4_DNR instance-data encoding.
This slice does not implement Neighbor Discovery encrypted DNS option padding or lifetime processing.
This slice does not implement an operating-system DHCP client or resolver selection policy.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The codec sits above the scalar RFC 9463 discovery option model and below any platform DHCP client integration. It gives ProtocolLab and future network adapters exact byte-level proof without moving DHCP state into the QUIC runtime.
